topic: AWG channel count and measured channel spacing
text: The 512-channel AWG was characterized by a wavelength scan. The measured average channel spacing was 0.093 nm.
The wavelength-to-pixel mapping shows multiple spectral orders. The bandwidth is 44 nm for the first order and 47.71 nm for the second order.
For the new coupling structure, an efficiency of more than 70% was measured in the higher wavelength range. The maximum variation throughout the entire wavelength range was 5%.
The output signals of 16 pixels are multiplexed to one successive-approximation switched-capacitor 12-bit (SAR) ADC with a sampling rate of 1.5 MS/s. The chip uses 32 integrated ADCs.
The SD-OCT system achieved a maximum sensitivity of 92 dB with 2.6 mW on the sample, an axial resolution of 13 µm in soft tissue (n=1.4), and a lateral resolution of 11 µm.
The acquisition speed of one A-scan is determined by the exposure control of the photodiodes and was set to 55 kHz.

topic: Measured signal roll-off and imaging depth
text: The measured 6 dB roll-off occurs at 2 mm, which covers almost the entire imaging depth of 2.2 mm in air.

topic: CMOS process and waveguide material stack
text: A 0.35 µm high-voltage CMOS process was used for the electronics. The waveguide stack comprises a 160 nm silicon-nitride (SiN) core separated from the photodiodes by a 7 µm silicon-dioxide (SiO2) layer; the top layer is 2 µm thick SiO2.

Light entering the input waveguide is distributed across the array of waveguides through the input coupler. Different path lengths in the phased array create wavelength-dependent phase delays. Each wavelength constructively interferes at a different position along the focal line of the output coupler; waveguides there collect specific wavelengths and guide them to corresponding photodiodes.

topic: Photodiode signal digitization in AWG diagram
text: The signals of 16 photodiodes are each buffered and digitized by an ADC.

topic: Aperiodic grating and taper coupling mechanism
text: The aperiodic grating ensures minimal back-coupling of reflected light into the waveguide. The integrated taper widens the mode field to match the photodiode and includes a grating taper to minimize reflections back into the waveguide.

A metal cage defines a confined optical environment. Light undergoes multiple reflections from the metal walls, redirecting it towards the photodiode and optimizing light collection and spatial localization.

topic: Residual coupling losses and wavelength variation
text: The losses primarily result from light passing through gaps between the metal cage and the photodiode. Simulations indicate that extending the metal cage further down to the photodiode could prevent almost all losses. The measured maximum variation throughout the wavelength range was 5%.

topic: ADC outputs and computer interface signal path
text: The outputs of the 32 ADCs are multiplexed to two 12-bit output busses, accompanied by camera-link protocol signals generated by the control logic. The chip is wire-bonded to a PCB, which transports the digital signal to the computer via a camera-link chip and connector.
The PIC is wire-bonded to the PCB, which features a camera-link connector for signal transmission to the computer via a frame grabber.

topic: Roll-off calculated from AWG channel spectral responses
text: The roll-off envelope is calculated from the spectral response functions of each AWG channel. These calculations reproduce the measured roll-off.

topic: Best-performing AWG channels predicted roll-off improvement
text: A simulated roll-off envelope using only the best 10% of channels with the lowest roll-off would improve the signal decay by 2.7 dB at 2 mm.

The roll-off simulation uses the spectral responses measured at each photodiode. Roll-off curves were calculated for all measured channels, the averaged spectral response, and the best-performing 10% of AWG channels.

For structural reconstruction, the data are sorted according to the camera-link protocol; the reference-arm-only background is subtracted; the spectrum is resampled to equally spaced wavenumbers; a Hanning window is applied; and a Fourier transform generates the A-scan depth information.

For OCTA, five B-scans are acquired at the same position. After the same post-processing steps, Gaussian blurring (sigma equals two) is applied, and speckle variance is calculated across repeated tomograms to retain signals that change over time, such as blood vessels.

Averaging over two or five B-scans makes the structural layers of the epidermis clearly distinguishable. Sweat ducts are visible even without averaging. No additional structural insights are obtained by averaging over 100 B-scans; a limited number of B-scans is therefore sufficient and reduces acquisition time.
The human-skin tomograms were acquired with a B-scan rate of 45.8 Hz (1200 A-scans per B-scan), corresponding to an acquisition time of 22 ms per B-scan.

topic: Coupling efficiency definition and measured range context
text: The waveguide-to-photodiode coupling measurements cover 800 nm to 900 nm. An efficiency of more than 70% is measured in the higher wavelength range, with a maximum variation of 5% throughout the entire measured wavelength range.
The authors report a coupling efficiency of 70% between the waveguide and photodiode in the wavelength range of 850 nm to 900 nm.

topic: AWG insertion loss and insertion loss uniformity definitions
text: Insertion loss (IL) of a channel is the power loss measured from the smallest peak of that channel's optical power within the entire spectrum to the 0-dB reference line. Insertion loss uniformity (ILU) is the difference between the maximum and minimum AWG insertion losses across all output channels.

topic: Simulated AWG ILU and insertion loss
text: For the 512-channel AWG, the design aimed for ILU = 1.5 dB and adjacent-channel crosstalk AX = 45 dB. The simulated AWG insertion loss reached 6 dB, of which 4 dB is attributed to non-uniformity ILU.
Adjacent-channel crosstalk (AX) is the power induced by a selected channel in its neighboring channel, and vice versa; the worst-case value across all channels defines AX.

Background crosstalk (BX) is the median peak optical power in the channel's BX band, which includes all wavelengths except those within the channel-center wavelength plus or minus the channel spacing.

The optimal exposure-time signal is a 55 kHz square wave with a 90% duty cycle, coupled with an ADC clock rate of 28 MHz with a 50% duty cycle. Exposure control influences photodiode integration time and also regulates data-transfer rate.

topic: Lateral and axial resolution measurement methods
text: Axial resolution is given by the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the point-spread function. Lateral resolution was assessed using a USAF resolution target (Thorlabs R3L3S1P), specifically group 6 element 4.

topic: Definitions of A-scan, B-scan and 3D volume
text: An A-scan is the depth profile of a single scanning position. Scanning over the sample acquires adjacent A-scans; scanning in one direction generates 2D B-scans, and scanning in two axes produces 3D volumes.
The exposure control also regulates the data-transfer rate. Higher data-transfer rates are constrained by the ADC capabilities, which are limited by the minimum time required for data transfer.

topic: Discussion of camera specifications and potential A-scan speed increase
text: The discussion states that imaging speed is determined by camera specifications. It also proposes more than two digital 12-bit output buses and a pipeline ADC with 25 MS/s sampling to increase the A-scan rate by a factor of 16, at the cost of higher power consumption and larger chip area.

Monolithically integrating the photodiodes with the AWG makes the system more robust and one step closer to maintenance-free operation. Remaining coupling losses arise mainly from gaps between the reflective metal cage and photodiode; fabrication limitations prevent extending the cage down to the photodiode.

topic: Potential full integration and permanent fiber attachment
text: The authors state that integrating an interferometer and SLD into the PIC could improve robustness and compactness. To create a completely maintenance-free system, the sample and reference fibers could be permanently attached or glued to the PIC.
The conclusion states that further improvements are needed to develop a small, robust, and commercially viable SD-OCT system.
The paper reports that the overall chip power consumption is 800 mW.

topic: Computer acquisition hardware and software identifiers
text: The acquired data are recorded using a frame grabber (Xcelera-CL-PX4-1) with a custom camera file (Teledyne Dalsa CamExpert). Acquisition and data processing are performed using MATLAB (R2020b, R2022b).
The discussion describes the 512-channel AWG as covering a bandwidth of 47 nm.
